title: Technology survey: inertia-locking retractors and self-retracting lifelines
context: RideBelt is an open, safety-critical Hee-Lee Oss project: an optional rider-worn backup restraint (low hip belt + short tethers; optional clip-on Shoulder Module or one-piece Integrated Harness) that latches into an open seat anchor standard (RAS). ALL safety content is DRAFT and not for use until a credentialed engineer signs off at the MVP gate (GOVERNANCE.md). Never remove a DRAFT banner, never give instructions for wearing or attaching anything to a ride, never copy text from paid standards (cite by number and title only), never name private individuals or incident victims, and respect the patent design-arounds in docs/research/patentability-fto.md. The arrest model makes slack the dominant variable, so self-retracting inertia-locking tethers are now preferred (concepts.md).
objective: Survey automotive seat-belt retractors and fall-protection self-retracting lifelines: locking principles, lock-up distance, rated loads, size and published standards, and assess fit to a 15–30 cm ride tether.
acceptanceCriteria: Lock-up distance data compared with the ≤ 2 cm slack target (REQ-L4)
Lists the patent families to check before any design (FTO note)
Every factual claim has a cited, working source link; estimates are labelled as estimates
